world.label: Pencil Supply Chain
world.summary: Businesses make, transport, and sell pencils through a recurring supply chain.

actions.description: Cut cedar and add logs to the loggers' stock.
The sawmill orders logs from the Oregon loggers.
Saw logs into cedar slats.
The factory orders cedar slats from the sawmill.
Mine graphite and add it to the miners' stock.
The lead maker orders graphite from the miners.
Produce clay for the lead maker's stock.
The lead maker orders clay from the clay supplier.
Mix graphite and clay into pencil leads.
The factory orders pencil leads from the lead maker.
Produce paint, brass ferrules, and erasers for the factory.
The factory orders paint, brass ferrules, and erasers from its supplier.
Produce boxes for the factory's stock.
The factory orders boxes from the box supplier.
Glue leads into slats, paint the pencils, and add brass ferrules and erasers.
Pack pencils into boxes from the factory's available stock.
The shop orders boxed pencils from the factory, with payment and delivery recorded.
The carrier delivers an arrived shipment of boxed pencils from the factory to the shop.
Sell a pencil from a shop to a customer and record the payment.

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: Oregon loggers turned cedar into logs, the mill made slats, and the lead maker and Pennsylvania factory made leads and pencils. Goods moved between suppliers, the factory, a carrier, and the country shop; the shop sold pencils to customers, though production sometimes waited for missing inputs.

mechanisms.name: Goods made from other goods
mechanisms.explanation: Oregon loggers made logs from cedar, the Oregon mill made slats from logs, the lead maker made leads from clay and graphite, and Pennsylvania factory assembled pencils from components.

mechanisms.name: Goods carried to the next step
mechanisms.explanation: Goods passed between businesses: the mill bought logs, the factory bought slats, and the carrier delivered boxed pencils to the country shop.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
mechanisms.explanation: The country shop sold pencils from its stock to waiting customers, reducing the waiting orders and giving pencils to customers.

mechanisms.name: Work held up

events.changed: nothing: refused because The requested amount is unavailable

mechanisms.explanation: Some work was held up by missing inputs. The factory reported needing slats and leads to resume production, and later bought those scarce components before making more pencils.
